issue_context.title: Feature: Drag folder onto "+" icon to create new tab
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem?**
It would be nice to be able to drag a folder onto the "+" icon for creating a new tab or onto a blank spot on the tab strip to create a new tab. Chrome/Edge/Firefox support doing this with links, and I have gotten used to doing it in browsers. When you try in Edge, a little arrow pops up too, which is a nice touch!
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/81886277/115799469-8e2acb80-a3a6-11eb-893f-74ed53320986.png)

**Describe the solution**
Implementing something like I described above would be nice!

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
CTRL+click on a folder to do this would work too, but both would be even better!

**Additional comment**
Thank you for the work y'all are putting into this app, it's amazing!
comments: possibly related to #4511 (Use CTRL + Left click for new tab)

Shouldn't the entire title bar act as a drop-point for folders to create new tabs?

A good example of something users will be familiar with could be to look at major browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, etc.) which allow you to drop links into the title bar to create a new tab. In fact, these include the possibility to place the new tab in a specific position using a small indicator:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7792033/177550604-c2f431c6-db09-4ed5-bcac-482b64bd6f01.png)
(Firefox)

Based on the browsers I have access to, it seems that the one spot that doesn't allow URL dropping in the browsers I have access to is the one with the system's minimize/maximize/close buttons.
This can be particularly useful for touch users.
Hi, I'd like to work on this. May I? Also I tried dragging a folder onto the "+" icon it shows the not allowed sign. How do I overcome that?
@ashrafmansuri you will have to add the dropped event.

> @ashrafmansuri you will have to add the dropped event.

I found the dropped event in BaseLayoutViewModel.cs but I'm not sure where exactly do I add it. Can you guide me a little?

Hi, can anyone help me with the dropped event? I tried but was unable to. Just the hints would do and I can take it from there.
Thanks.

Working on the feature right now. Having issues as adding the AllowDrop and Drop flags to the TabBar elements doesn't seem to change their behavior with dropped folders. I am also reading up on the UI XAML behavior [here](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/api/windows.ui.xaml.uielement.drop?view=winrt-22621), but haven't been able to figure out why it doesn't trigger the Drop event yet.

Alright think I am figuring it out, Drop was never called until one of the Drag events was handled it seems. I will explore this some more and see if I can get the drag and drop to trigger properly

EDIT:
Seem to have figured out the dragged event system. Turns out you must set a DataPackageOperation to something, otherwise the Drop event is not triggered. 
Expect a pull request with the feature in the next couple days
